text:
Gregor: kicked off an nsys capture against the small repro to pin down that KV write spike. attached perfetto export when it's done.
Maya: can you paste the exact nsys command so I can run locally? :eyes:
Gregor: sure —
```
nsys profile --output=nsys_run1 --trace=cuda,cudnn,osrt --sample=cpu --capture-range=nvtx --force-overwrite --stats=true \
  --cpuctxsw=true --duration=90 python repro/kv_write_spike.py
```
Maya: thanks. quick summary from the trace: flash_attn_fused_v3 kernels alternate with short kv_write kernels, and the writes bunch up at the end of micro-batches causing stalls. timeline shows GPU SM occupancy dips right when write bursts happen.
Kevin: interesting. my initial thought — the kernel selector switches to fused flash when seq_len>128 and peak_throughput looks better, but it doesn't factor in per-request kv write ratio or write contention. so we get a compute-optimal kernel that is write-unfriendly.
Ana: ran a short nvprof pass, here's the snippet that lines up:
```
GPU activities:
  1234  flash_attn_fused_v3   time(ms)=12.8  SM_util=85%  avg_reg=... 
   78  kv_cache_write         time(ms)=3.4   memcpy_kind=async  HtoD=0.9MB
   82  kv_cache_read          time(ms)=1.1
```
Ana: writes aren't huge individually, but they cluster and serialize due to how we schedule the small memcpy+kernel combos.
Gregor: perfetto link: https://perfetto.dev/trace/xxxx (uploaded). You can see the small H2D slices overlaid on the fused kernels. The fused kernel layout seems to rely on contiguous KV buffers; our current prefetch doesn't keep writes isolated so we pay lock-step stalls.
Maya: rough mitigation idea: teach the kernel chooser to consider a write_bias metric. if kv_write_bytes / total_token_bytes > 0.12 prefer legacy_attn_kern (slightly lower compute perf but nicer write overlap).
Kevin: alternatively, try a scheduling tweak: when microbatch variance > 30% do a quick request reshuffle to group heavy-write items together so writes can be coalesced/serialized intentionally rather than interleaved. Gregor: I tried that locally — grouped by estimated kv_write_bytes — tail latency dropped ~12% on the repro.
Gregor: local numbers: baseline p99=274ms, with reshuffle p99=241ms, with kernel-heuristic change p99=233ms. throughput impact negligible.
Ana: the nvprof output also showed memcpy async queuing on the same stream as some kernels. if we move writes to a dedicated copy stream and synchronize less aggressively we might hide some H2D. but need careful correctness checks for KV lifetime.
Maya: PR opened: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/4321 — implements write_bias in KernelPolicy and a small reshuffle operator in the scheduler. includes unit tests and microbenchmarks. :thumbsup:
Kevin: good. I'll run an overnight nsys sweep across the mixed workload matrix (seq_len 64/128/256, batch skews 10/30/50%) and check regressions. if all green, canary on dedicated pools next week.
perf-bot: canary deploy scheduled for 2026-03-19T02:00:00Z (canary/dedicated/gpu-pool-07).
Maya: also adding a perfetto trace check to our CI smoke so we can catch similar write-clustering patterns earlier. small NSEC detector to flag repeated H2D bursts during token generation.
Kevin: thx team. next actions: (1) overnight nsys runs, (2) load test PR on staging, (3) review copy-stream correctness. assign owners in PR.
Gregor: assigning reviewers now. will post nsys logs in this thread when ready.
Maya: nice work — this felt like a low-noise/root-cause instead of chasing random scheduler noise. :smile:
